prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create a square watercolor storyboard, ideally 1536×1536, exactly TWO columns by THREE rows, six independent 3:2 LANDSCAPE panels in row-major order. Equal cells with a narrow clear ivory paper gap, no borders, labels or frames; no scene crosses a cell boundary. Keep the full primary subject inside the central 82% of each cell.
MEDIUM ONLY is shared: sophisticated adult editorial watercolor on warm ivory cold-pressed paper, transparent layered washes, expressive pencil contours, irregular pigment edges softly dissolving into unpainted paper. Sage, terracotta, lavender, soft ochre with scene-appropriate blues and greens. Loose believable anatomy and gestures, not photographic, not 3D, not cartoon. Warm and adult, but do NOT impose golden sunshine or a cozy room on every setting.
Each panel illustrates the SPECIFIC QUESTION supplied, not merely the topic. Make the action or idea readable without a caption. Change the subject, action, setting, scale or viewpoint substantially for every panel. A close crop of a prop from the preceding scene is not a new concept. Use the concrete directions below, no decorative filler or invented extra scenes.
Fictional adults and natural hands/gestures are welcome where specified; use candid back/side/over-shoulder views or crop naturally above the chin, never blank faceless heads. No idealized romance, no default gender roles, no recognizable real person. Adults of ordinary appearance, varied skin tones. These are fictional examples, not reconstructions of a user's memories. Emotion can be mixed; do not visually assert reconciliation or a promised outcome.
STRICTLY NO cups, mugs, drinking glasses, plates, cutlery, kettles, table settings, flower vases, decorative bouquets, hearts, rings, floating icons, puzzle metaphors, UI, captions, letters, numbers, handwriting, logos or watermarks. No café, Tuscan room or wicker furniture unless expressly requested. Book pages, maps, tickets and screens must have no readable writing. Do not fill unrelated panels with the same furniture, fabric or object.
The fictional couple are two ordinary adult men in their late forties, different builds and skin tones. Natural playful behavior, no stock romance, no idealized athletic bodies.
STORY S11: A Saturday just for us
PANEL 1
Question context (do not render as text): If we had a whole Saturday free, how would you like to start it with me?
Recognition cue: A slow free morning
Paint: Two adults' socked feet peep from rumpled bed sheets in soft morning light, one relaxed hand reaches to silence a plain unnumbered alarm clock. A free Saturday beginning slowly, no breakfast objects.
PANEL 2
Question context (do not render as text): Where would you like our free Saturday to take us next?
Recognition cue: Where the day takes us
Paint: Two adults cycle at an easy pace along a local riverside path, wide open sky and a simple footbridge ahead; an ordinary nearby outing, varied scene-appropriate blue-green watercolor rather than a luxury trip.
PANEL 3
Question context (do not render as text): What silly thing could we add to our Saturday just for fun?
Recognition cue: Something silly just for fun
Paint: One adult makes a ridiculous sock puppet peek from behind a low sofa while their partner laughs from the floor, a candid playful indoor moment. The handmade puppet has simple stitched eyes, no cartoon mascot or lettering.
PANEL 4
Question context (do not render as text): How would you like our free Saturday to end?
Recognition cue: How the day ends
Paint: Back view of two adults comfortably sprawled on floor cushions watching an improvised film projected onto a plain wall at night; the fictional projection is only loose monochrome dancing shapes, no recognizable film or text. Quiet chosen ending.
PANEL 5
Question context (do not render as text): Which small part of our made-up Saturday would you like to try?
Recognition cue: One small piece to try for real
Paint: Close outdoor scene of two adults spreading a small blanket on the grass at a nearby patch of park, jackets still on and bikes just out of focus; a tiny accessible part of the imagined day, no whole-day itinerary.
PANEL 6
Question context (do not render as text): If you like, keep one scene from our made-up Saturday.
Recognition cue: A scene from our made-up day
Paint: A small hand-painted memory vignette of the sock puppet peeking out of a cycling jacket pocket beside the folded park blanket, playful unexpected detail from this specific imagined Saturday, no cups or dining objects.
